text:
tess: quick heads-up: after the compact-route header change, a few tenants reported their per-intent quota dashboards showing almost no traffic for the `signup` intent. total requests unchanged. anyone seen this pattern?
omar: yep, saw it in traces. shim is normalizing headers but seems to drop the second `x-route` value in the proxy path.
rachel: can you paste a reproducer?
tess: reproducer: `curl -H "x-route: tenant=bright" -H "x-route: intent=signup" https://api.redwood.prod/v1/complete` 3 ingestion shows tenant but no intent.
omar: impact: sampling keys and quota attribution use `route.intent`, so losing it collapses metrics into DEFAULT buckets.
rachel: mitigation options: 1) revert shim 2) server merge multi-valued `x-route` 3) SDK emit fallback header `x-route-json` (JSON map) 4) console ingest fallback.
tess: shortest path is SDK fallback + ingest change. put it behind opt-in env var so we can coordinate.
omar: agree. SDKs: py/ts/go add when multiple `x-route` headers present, set `x-route-json: {"tenant":"...","intent":"..."}` if ROUTE_JSON_FALLBACK=1.
rachel: obs can wire ingestion to parse `x-route-json` within 48h behind canary. Will read it only if `x-route` lacks keys.
tess: dev-bot can you create a 5% canary and flip env var for that cohort? also link tickets.
dev-bot: created canary group `route-json-fallback-5pct`. Linked ENG-RT-4991 and INGEST-1017. Canary scheduled in 30m.
infrastructure: note that some proxies may strip quotes; SDKs should URL-encode header value or provide a compact fallback `x-route-kv: tenant=bright;intent=signup`.
omar: good point. add `x-route-kv` as fallback in SDKs for mobile stacks.
rachel: monitoring reqs: compare sampled trace counts where logs include `intent` vs telemetry `intent` during canary; alert if mismatch > 10%.
tess: i'll open SDK PRs today with unit tests and docs. keep header keys lowercase. don't change existing `x-route` behavior.
omar: long-term follow-up: change shim to merge instead of overwrite and remove fallback after 2 weeks of stable parity.
tess: thanks. i'll post updates to #incidents and tag product ops.
